newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen apt to add reserves but forecasts differ.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen apt to add reserves but forecasts differ.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is apt to add reserves to the banking system on Tuesday, but analysts' views of the Fed's options were wide-ranging.

"One way or the other the Fed's going to be adding reserves," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president and money market economist at Dean Witter Reynolds. "We lean toward a (temporary reserve addition through) system (repurchase agreements), but it's possible that if they don't do a system, they'll give you (a permanent reserve addition through) a coupon pass instead."
"A coupon pass is so hard to predict," said Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A. "Another round is coming -- I just don't know when."
But Stiles noted that with Federal funds trading at 5-1/4 percent, the Fed's target for the rate, the open market operations desk might just do another overnight system.
"You got funds right on target," said Stiles. "They did an overnight (system) yesterday. Chances are they'll do another overnight system RP today."
With funds trading on target, the Fed might also refrain from open market operations on Tuesday, some analysts said.
"I couldn't rule out their staying out," said Stiles.

"I think they can stay out of the market, but there's a possiblity they might begin to address next week's add need with a term system repurchase operation," said Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co. "I think there's little, if any, reserve need today. But they might want to get a leg up on next week with a six- or nine-day system."
Thrapp said a permanent reserve addition with the Fed buying coupons "remains possible at any time."
At 1000 EST/1500 GMT, Federal funds were trading at 5-1/4 percent, the Fed's target for the rate.
(( -- E. Freilich, North American Treasury Desk 212-859-1679))
